platforms.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio — May 2026 notable-changes wave (new vs. cached April 2026 baseline)
details: **Agent inventory schema** — Discover and audit all Copilot Studio agents in the tenant from the admin center, the Power Platform API, or **Azure Resource Graph**. Per-agent metadata includes creator, last-published time, deployed channels, authentication method, and capabilities; covers draft and published agents (excludes V1/Classic bots), refreshed roughly every 20 minutes. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-agent-inventory

**Computer use is now generally available** + new **computer use standalone tools (preview)** — Computer Use (CUA-powered web/desktop UI automation on Windows) moved from preview to GA; standalone computer-use tools add modular, reusable UI-automation tools with built-in governance, model selection, and observability. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/computer-use

**New agent-flow / workflow nodes** — **Microsoft 365 Copilot node** sends prompts to Microsoft 365 Copilot or a specific agent from within a workflow (research/audit-drafting automation); **Prompt node** makes a single AI call with dynamic content and per-node model selection. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/microsoft-365-copilot-node-workflow

Also in the May wave (noted, not raised as findings): consent-based recording for voice agents, asynchronous (long-running) agent-flow responses, a consolidated agent readiness/issue-status page (preview), and **Mistral Medium 3.5** as an experimental primary model. Microsoft Entra agent identities (preview) also appears but was already cached as a Nov 2025 item. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI) — Codex CLI 0.137.0 (June 4, 2026)
details: **Hosted web and image tools in code-mode flows** with parallel web search; **Multi-agent v2** with runtime-choice persistence per thread; **remote-control clients can manage pairing and controller grants via app-server RPCs**; enterprise/admin flows now surface monthly credit limits and **cloud-managed config bundles**; plugin workflows gained machine-readable JSON output and cached remote catalog suggestions. (Codex app 26.602, same day, added activity insights/share cards and Computer Use startup-readiness hardening.) Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

platforms.name: Cursor — 3.7 + Enterprise Organizations (June 3–4, 2026) [watching tier]
details: **Enterprise Organizations (GA)** — a new top-level **Organization** container above Teams, plus **Groups** (lightweight user cohorts that cut across/within teams). Each carries its own security, governance, budget, **model access**, spend limits, and **agent permissions**; org-level identity management and a spend/token rollup across teams; users move between teams via dashboard/API/CSV ("most permissive setting wins" on overlap). Source: https://cursor.com/changelog/enterprise-organizations

**3.7 (June 4)** Canvas Design Mode (annotate UI elements in canvases), interactive context-usage report, full-screen canvas sharing, and agent-embedded buttons that trigger specific prompts. Source: https://cursor.com/changelog

findings.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio Agent inventory schema
findings.description: A new tenant-wide agent inventory lets admins discover and audit every Copilot Studio / Agent Builder agent via the Power Platform admin center, the Power Platform API, and **Azure Resource Graph**, exposing per-agent metadata (creator, last-published time, deployed channels, authentication method, capabilities) for both draft and published agents. This is a first-class inventory/discovery surface that AISPM should ingest directly — it is effectively the platform's own agent inventory feed and the authoritative source for mapping Copilot Studio agents as entities, their owners, channels, and auth posture, and for flagging toxic combinations (e.g., unauthenticated/anonymous-channel agents, orphaned-owner agents, or agents with broad capabilities). AISPM must consume this schema to keep Copilot Studio agent coverage complete

findings.title: Copilot Studio Computer Use GA + standalone computer-use tools
findings.description: Computer Use (CUA-powered automation that controls browsers and Windows desktop apps on a user's behalf) moved to general availability, and a new **standalone computer-use tool** type adds modular, reusable UI-automation tools with their own governance, model selection, and observability. This expands an existing capability into a discrete, reusable inventory entity: AISPM should map standalone computer-use tools (and the agents/flows that attach them) and treat a Computer-Use-enabled agent — which can click, type, and read any on-screen content with built-in credentials — as a high-privilege, GUI-level execution path subject to AIRT testing for prompt-injection-driven unintended actions

findings.title: Copilot Studio Microsoft 365 Copilot node + Prompt node (new agent-flow building blocks)
findings.description: Two new workflow/agent-flow nodes shipped in May. The **Microsoft 365 Copilot node** lets a workflow send prompts to Microsoft 365 Copilot (or a specific agent) and consume the result — a new agent-to-Copilot data flow that can pull tenant grounding data into automated processes. The **Prompt node** makes a single inline AI call with dynamic content and per-node model selection. AISPM should add these node types to its Copilot Studio flow inventory and map the M365 Copilot node as a new data-flow edge (workflow → M365 Copilot → grounded enterprise data), which AIDR should also treat as a new activity/data-flow surface

findings.title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.137.0 — hosted web/image tools in code-mode, Multi-agent v2, remote-control grant management
findings.description: The June 4 Codex CLI release lets code-mode flows use hosted web and image tools with parallel web search (new autonomous web-egress/tool surface from inside code execution), adds Multi-agent v2 with per-thread runtime-choice persistence (expanded local multi-agent orchestration), and lets remote-control clients manage pairing and controller grants via app-server RPCs (a remote-control authorization surface), plus cloud-managed config bundles for enterprise/admin. ENDPOINT should track Codex CLI installs that can now reach the web and spawn persistent multi-agent runs locally, and treat remote-control pairing/controller grants as a new device-access surface on monitored machines

findings.title: Cursor Enterprise Organizations (new org/group governance & identity entities)
findings.description: Cursor (watching tier) added a generally-available **Organization** layer above Teams plus cross-cutting **Groups**, each with its own security, governance, budget, **model access**, spend limits, and **agent permissions**, org-level identity management, and a spend/token rollup. These introduce new governance/identity entities for a monitored endpoint AI tool: AISPM should map Cursor organizations, teams, and groups — and especially per-group model access and agent permissions — since "most permissive setting wins" on overlapping membership can silently grant a user broader model/agent capability than their primary team allows (a privilege-aggregation toxic combination)

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI) — Codex enterprise expansion (June 2, 2026)
details: **Codex "Sites" (preview, Business/Enterprise) — agent-built, OpenAI-hosted web apps & dashboards**: The Codex app's new Sites plugin turns a prompt or compatible project into a deployed site hosted by OpenAI — websites, dashboards, internal tools, web apps, planners, review workspaces, project boards, galleries, and games. Sites hosts projects that build Cloudflare Worker–compatible output as ES modules. Workflow: validate the build → save a deployable version for review → deploy the approved version. Each project has its own hosted environment variables and secrets (managed in the Sites panel), a deployment status, a workspace-shareable URL, and access controls the agent can change ("change who can access a deployed site"). Rolling out to Business and Enterprise plans first, with enterprise admin enablement via role-based access control. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/sites

**Codex on ChatGPT for iOS 1.2026.146 — SSH to Windows + biometric lock**: Adds SSH connection support so the mobile Codex app can connect to Windows machines, an optional Face ID/passcode lock for Codex, and a settings screen for follow-up behavior and code diff preferences. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

findings.title: OpenAI Codex "Sites" — agent-deployed, OpenAI-hosted applications
findings.description: As of June 2, 2026 (preview, Business/Enterprise), the Codex app's Sites plugin lets a Codex agent create, save, deploy, and inspect full websites, dashboards, internal tools, web apps, and games **hosted by OpenAI** (Cloudflare Worker–compatible ES-module output). Each Site is a new inventory entity carrying its own hosted environment variables and secrets, a deployment lifecycle (saved → approved → deployed), a workspace-shareable URL, and access controls the agent itself can modify. AISPM must discover and map these new entities — Codex Sites projects, their stored secrets/env vars, deployment status, and sharing/access scope — and flag toxic combinations such as an agent that both holds secrets and can deploy a publicly reachable app *and* widen its audience (an agent-controlled exposure/exfiltration path). This is an entirely new service surface, not an extension of an existing one

findings.title: Codex Sites as a new agent-controlled deployment/exposure attack surface
findings.description: Because a Codex agent can deploy live, OpenAI-hosted endpoints and change who can access them, a prompt-injected or misdirected Codex session becomes a vector to stand up or repoint a public web app, embed/exfiltrate secrets via a Site's stored environment variables, or broaden a Site's audience without human review. AIRT should add Codex Sites deploy/share/secret-management actions to its red/purple-team surface for OpenAI agents — testing prompt-injection paths that result in unauthorized deployment, audience widening, or secret exposure

findings.title: Codex (ChatGPT iOS 1.2026.146) adds SSH connections to Windows machines
findings.description: The June 2, 2026 ChatGPT iOS release adds SSH connection support so the mobile Codex app can connect to Windows machines (alongside an optional Face ID/passcode lock for Codex). This extends Codex's remote-execution reach — previously remote control / Computer Use on Windows — to direct SSH sessions into Windows hosts from a mobile device. ENDPOINT should treat a mobile Codex install with SSH access to Windows endpoints as a new remote-execution/credential surface on monitored machines

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI) — Codex CLI & SDKs
details: **Codex CLI 0.136.0 (June 1, 2026) — native Amazon Bedrock backend**: The local Codex agent can now run against Amazon Bedrock with AWS-managed authentication (Bedrock API key via `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`/`AWS_REGION`, or the standard AWS SDK credential chain — `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`/`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, shared config, or console creds — with SigV4 signing). Same release also adds session archiving via the `/archive` command and Windows sandbox provisioning with an elevated setup path. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/amazon-bedrock

**OpenAI Python v2.40.0 / Node v6.41.0 (June 1, 2026) — Amazon Bedrock Responses support**: The official SDKs add a first-class Bedrock client so the Responses API can be pointed at the `bedrock-mantle` OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws/v1`) authenticated with a Bedrock API key instead of an OpenAI key. The immediately prior releases (Python v2.39.0 / Node v6.40.0, also June 1) added workload identity in audit logs, additional tools in responses, and made `ActionSearch.query` optional. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock

findings.title: OpenAI SDKs & Codex CLI add native Amazon Bedrock provider (cross-cloud inference routing)
findings.description: As of June 1, 2026, the official `openai-python` v2.40.0, `openai-node` v6.41.0, and Codex CLI 0.136.0 all ship turnkey "Amazon Bedrock Responses support," letting OpenAI's standard client libraries and the local Codex agent send Responses/Chat traffic to AWS Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible `bedrock-mantle` endpoint authenticated with AWS credentials (Bedrock API key or IAM/SigV4) rather than an `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The underlying OpenAI-on-Bedrock integration has been GA since April 2026, but moving it into the default SDKs and CLI makes it the path of least resistance and breaks several monitoring assumptions: detection keyed on "OpenAI SDK ⇒ api.openai.com" now misses inference that terminates at AWS Bedrock; a single OpenAI-shaped agent may straddle two monitored clouds; and a developer endpoint running Codex can hold AWS credentials and open a new egress path to `bedrock-mantle.*.api.aws`. AIDR should treat OpenAI-client / Codex traffic to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint as a monitored cross-provider data flow (and attribute it to the OpenAI SDK rather than a generic AWS call), while ENDPOINT-side inventory should flag Codex installs configured with the `amazon-bedrock` model provider as holding AWS credentials with a Bedrock egress path. New toxic combination: a Codex endpoint with broad AWS IAM credentials plus the Bedrock provider can route prompt/response data — including injected instructions — into the customer's own AWS account, blending agent traffic with first-party AWS API activity

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI) — Codex
details: **Codex 26.527 (May 29, 2026) — Computer Use on Windows**: The Codex app can now operate graphical desktop applications on Windows by seeing, clicking, and typing in the foreground (install the Computer Use plugin, then invoke with `@Computer` or `@AppName`). Remote control from the ChatGPT app on iOS/Android is extended to Windows devices, so a user can steer or send follow-up instructions to a Windows machine running Codex from their phone. Also added: a profile section surfacing usage stats and token activity, and thread-coordination improvements for local projects and worktrees. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/windows

platforms.name: Cursor
details: **Cursor 3.6 (May 29, 2026) — Auto-review Run Mode**: A new agent run mode (Settings → Agents → Run Mode) that allows the agent to work longer with fewer approval prompts. It applies to **Shell, MCP, and Fetch** tool calls: allowlisted calls run immediately, sandboxable calls execute in an isolated sandbox, and all other actions are routed to a **classifier subagent** that decides whether to allow the call, try a different approach, or ask the user for approval. The classifier can be steered with custom instructions. Source: https://cursor.com/changelog/auto-review

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — Computer Use on Windows + mobile remote control
findings.description: Codex 26.527 extends agentic computer use (previously Mac-only) to Windows. The Codex app can now take over the active Windows desktop — moving the pointer, typing, and operating any foreground app the user allows — and can be steered remotely from the ChatGPT mobile app even while the user is away from the machine. This is a new endpoint attack surface on a new OS: a local AI agent that drives the GUI of arbitrary applications (browsers, app settings, data sources with no API) with the logged-in user's full desktop privileges. ENDPOINT must inventory Codex installs that have the Computer Use plugin enabled as distinct desktop-control capabilities per host, capture which apps are allow-listed (including "Always allow" grants that suppress future per-task prompts), and attribute GUI-level actions to the agent rather than the human. New toxic combinations: an "Always allow" grant on a sensitive app (email, finance, admin console) combined with mobile remote control means a prompt-injected or hijacked Codex session can act against that app's UI unattended, with no terminal/CLI trace — Codex's own docs note it can't automate terminal apps or itself, so GUI-driven actions are the bypass path

findings.title: Cursor — Auto-review Run Mode (reduced-approval Shell/MCP/Fetch execution)
findings.description: Cursor 3.6 adds a run mode that lets the agent execute Shell, MCP, and Fetch tool calls without per-call human approval. Allowlisted calls run immediately, sandboxable calls run isolated, and the remainder are gated by an AI **classifier subagent** instead of a human. This removes the human from the loop for a large class of tool executions — including arbitrary shell commands and outbound fetches — on the developer endpoint. ENDPOINT (watching tier) should treat Auto-review as a distinct, higher-autonomy execution posture per Cursor install: record whether it is enabled, the configured allowlist of immediately-running Shell/MCP/Fetch operations, and any custom classifier instructions (which themselves become a prompt-injection / policy-weakening target). New toxic combination: a permissive allowlist plus a steerable classifier means an agent can run shell commands, reach MCP servers, and exfiltrate via Fetch with only an LLM — not a person — deciding what is safe
